tex_content.label: shortpi2triv
tex_content.html:
Let $(X,g)$ be compact with $\pi _2(X)=0$. There is $\zeta >0$ such that every family $\Gamma \colon S^2\to \Lambda X$ whose loops all have length below $\zeta $ represents zero in $\pi _3(X)$.
Proof

\sketch Choose $\zeta $ below the injectivity radius. Join each point of each loop to its value at a fixed parameter by the unique short geodesic. These geodesics give a continuous family of spanning disks and deform $\Gamma $ to a family of constant loops. That remaining family is null-homotopic because $\pi _2(X)=0$.

□

Corollary
[Short loops bound small-area disks]
